Lexi Conquest: Español (España), dataset es-ES-rla-2.9-wiktionary-wordfreq-v1

Accepted spelling forms
Recursos Lingüísticos Abiertos del Español (RLA-es), release 2.9.
https://github.com/sbosio/rla-es/tree/ea82c1214ead57740798acf66a1e18e5ac874c41
https://github.com/sbosio/rla-es/releases/download/v2.9/es_ES.xpi
Original es-ES.aff and es-ES.dic are retained here unmodified, together with
upstream README and license texts. This project chooses MPL 1.1 from the
upstream MPL/GPL/LGPL options. The generated spelling lists are modifications
of these sources and remain covered by MPL 1.1. Their source and generator
are available in the repository. nspell 2.1.5 (MIT) is build-only, not shipped
as runtime code. The dictionary records spellings, not regional commonness.

Answer selection and dictionary meanings
Wiktionary contributors, Spanish-language Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0.
https://es.wiktionary.org/
https://kaikki.org/dictionary/rawdata.html
Retained evidence was extracted by Wiktextract and distributed by Kaikki.
The Spanish-edition raw artifacts do not supply exact source-page revisions.
Per-entry raw-line hashes and word source links remain in the shared evidence.
The original pinned 4–7-letter and extended extracts and artifact hashes are
recorded in src/data/spanish/selection-source.json and extended-source.json.
The Spain pack reuses those extracts under their original license; it does
not claim that those mixed-region data were acquired specifically for Spain.
Definitions are abridged, formatting is removed, supplied labels are retained,
and answer senses are filtered and ordered for Spain. They are Spanish text,
not English translations or Mexico-context AI-authored lessons.

wordfreq 3.0.2, Robyn Speer and contributors, data CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT.
https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/tree/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b
Full wordfreq acknowledgments and underlying source credits, including
SUBTLEX, are retained in ../spanish-selection/wordfreq-README.md, with its MIT
license alongside it. General Spanish spelling frequencies are not
Spain-specific, current, or sense-specific frequency measurements.

The combined answer selection, meanings and adaptation metadata are under
CC BY-SA 4.0. A copy is included here. See src/data/spanish-spain/source.json,
review.json, coverage.json, and scripts/generate-spanish-spain.mjs for exact
pinned inputs, modifications and reproducible output checksums. Reproduce
with: node scripts/generate-spanish-spain.mjs --check

Limitations
The reused lexical extraction was scoped to Mexican-dictionary accepted
spellings at Zipf >= 3.5. An es-ES spelling absent from that evidence remains
a valid guess but cannot automatically become an answer. All selected answers
have bundled source meanings; broader guess definitions are incomplete.
Source regional labels and model review are not native-human certification.
Other-region and grammatical labels may appear in guess-only definitions.
Accents, Ü and Ñ remain distinct. The Mexico pack is unchanged.
